title: Pineapple Tallow Balm: I Put Beef Fat on My Face and It Worked
body:
Okay so look. I was scrolling on my phone, battery at like 12%, and I saw this thing about a tallow balm. Beef tallow. For your skin. My first thought was, obviously, what. You mean like… cooking fat? From a cow? To put on your face? I was half-watching some baking show in the background and the whole thing felt ridiculous. But my skin was being so difficult last spring—flaky, tight, just angry for no reason—and the expensive stuff in the fancy jar wasn’t doing anything. So I was curious. Annoyed, but curious. I ended up getting this Whipped Tallow Balm in Pineapple from this little Etsy shop, mostly because “pineapple” sounded way less intimidating than “beef fat.” And honestly? It’s weird. But it works. I don’t know how else to say it.

## How I Even Started Using Tallow on My Face

It started with my elbows. They were like sandpaper. I tried everything. Lotions, creams, that thick stuff in the blue tub. Nothing. It would feel okay for an hour and then back to desert mode. I remembered my grandma used to have this tin of something she’d put on her hands in winter. It smelled like… lard and roses? I don’t know. She swore by it. So when I saw this tallow skincare thing, that memory popped up. I figured, grandma wisdom has to count for something, right? Even if it sounds gross.

I did a quick search. Like, five minutes while my coffee was microwaving. The science-y bit, the part that made me go “hmm,” is that grass-fed beef tallow is supposed to be really similar to the oils our skin makes naturally. Sebum, or whatever. So it absorbs deep instead of just sitting on top. It made a sort of sense. Our bodies recognize it. Way more than some lab-made chemical with fifteen syllables. I was still skeptical. Very. But my elbows were winning the war, so I clicked buy. The whole thing felt like a weird experiment.

## What This Pineapple Tallow Balm Actually Does

It arrived on a Tuesday. Maybe Wednesday. The weather had just started to turn, that weird spring mix of warm sun and cold wind that ruins your skin. The jar was small. Cute. I opened it and poked it. The texture was… strange. Not bad strange. It’s whipped, so it’s light but dense? You scoop a little and it melts from your finger heat. It goes on kind of oily for a second, and then it’s just gone. Absorbed. That was the first surprise. No greasy film. My hands just felt… normal. But better normal. Hydrated without being sticky.

The smell. Right. The pineapple scent. It doesn’t smell like beef. At all. Which was my biggest fear. It smells like… a tropical fruit candy from when you were a kid, but not in a cheap way. Sweet. Bright. Cheerful. It’s a vacation feeling in a jar. It made the whole “putting cow fat on my skin” thing way less psychologically weird. I started with my elbows and my knuckles, which were cracked. Within a couple days, the cracks were just… gone. The sandpaper elbows were smoothing out. I got brave and tried it on my face before bed. I was sure I’d wake up with a new zit colony. But I didn’t. My skin just felt calm. Quiet. For the first time in months.

## My Skin After a Few Weeks of This Stuff

So I kept using it. Morning and night. The ritual of it became nice. The little pineapple smell to start the day. My skin stopped freaking out. That tight, itchy feeling after washing my face? Gone. The dry patches around my nose that makeup would cling to? History. I started using it on my lips too—just a tiny dab—and my tube of lip balm got lonely in the drawer. I even put a bit on a cut on my hand and it healed up faster. I’m not a doctor. I don’t know why. It just did.

Here’s the real test: I was visiting my mom and she grabbed my hand and said “your skin is so soft, what are you using?” And I had to tell her. “Uh, it’s like, a balm. Made from beef fat. But it smells like pineapple!” She made a face. The exact face I made when I first heard of it. I let her try it. She stole my jar. Now she has her own. The circle of life, I guess. The benefits of tallow skincare, for real, are just that it works with your skin, not against it. It’s simple. No twenty-step routine. Just one thing that does a lot.

## Would I Buy This Tallow Balm Again?

Yeah. I already did. I’m on my second jar. The first one lasted me a good while, you only need a tiny bit. I got mine from that Etsy shop, the one that makes it in France. It feels like a proper little craft thing, not a mass-produced bottle from a factory. Knowing it’s just simple, natural ingredients from grass-fed cows… it matters. It feels less like slapping a random cream on and more like actually nourishing your skin. The whole thing has made me rethink what I put on my body. If my great-grandma could use it, why did we ever stop?

Anyway. My skin’s happy. I’m happy. That’s all I wanted. If you’re staring at your screen feeling skeptical about putting beef tallow on your face, I get it. I was you. But if your skin is being difficult and nothing else is clicking, it might be worth a shot. It’s just one of those things you have to try to get. It’s not magic. It’s just… really good, simple stuff.

## Quick Questions I Get Asked

**Is beef tallow good for your face?**
Weirdly, yes. Because it’s so close to the oils our skin already makes, it sinks right in and helps balance everything out. It doesn’t just sit on top and pretend. It’s like giving your skin something it actually recognizes and knows how to use.

**Does tallow balm clog pores?**
I was terrified of this. But no, not for me. Because it absorbs so deeply, it doesn’t just clog stuff up. It’s non-comedogenic. My skin actually cleared up a bit, I think because it was finally properly hydrated and stopped overproducing oil to compensate.

**What does the pineapple tallow balm smell like?**
Like summer. Seriously. It’s a sweet, fruity, cheerful smell—like a ripe pineapple, but not fake or overwhelming. It completely covers any “animal fat” scent, which is genius. It just makes you happy when you put it on. No weird kitchen vibes at all.

So yeah. That’s my tallow balm story. My elbows are smooth, my face is calm, and I smell like a tropical drink. Not bad for a Tuesday night experiment.
